plugins.description: Global memory and user-level system prompts for DeepSeek Harness: cross-session facts with a per-turn index that costs no context.
plugins.readme_text: # dsh-memory-system-prompt **中文** | [English](#english) 全局记忆插件：AI 可以主动把事实写进记忆文件，并在后续对话里按需读取。记忆索引每轮自动注入系统提示，**不占用对话上下文**。 同时包含**用户级系统提示词**功能（原先独立的 `dsh-system-prompt` 已并入本包），两部分共用同一个设置页。 ## 它解决什么 模型本身没有跨会话记忆。这个插件给出一份可持久、可检索的记忆区： - **AI 主动写**：对话中发现的稳定事实（偏好、约定、环境细节）由模型调用工具写入； - **索引常驻**：每轮把「标题 + 一句话摘要」注入系统提示，模型知道有什么； - **正文按需**：需要细节时再调工具读全文，不把整个记忆库塞进上下文； - **可按对话关**：某个对话不想带记忆时，单独关掉。 ## 工具 | 工具 | 作用 | |---|---| | `memory_save` | 保存或更新一条记忆（同名覆盖） | | `memory_read` | 按标识读取一条记忆的正文 | | `memory_list` | 列出全部记忆（默认只返回索引） | | `memory_delete` | 删除一条记忆 | ## 用户级系统提示词 写一次，对所有对话生效；也可以按对话单独禁用。 - **自定义正文**：任何想长期强加给模型的要求（语气、格式、禁止事项）； - **九维风格档位**：不想写长文时，用档位拼出一段行为指令（基础语气、亲切程度、热情程度、表情符号、可视化回答、标题和列表、快速回答、提示词建议、回答长度）； - **两种注入位置**：作为系统提示的一部分，或作为上下文片段。 档位默认都是「默认」，全部保持默认时不产生任何额外内容。 ## 界面 - **输入框左侧开关**：三态（关 / 部分 / 开），按对话生效； - **设置 → 记忆与提示词**：管理全局开关、单条记忆、系统提示词与风格档位、首次使用引导。 ## 存储 | 路径 | 内容 | |---|---| | `~/.dsh/memory/` | 每条记忆一个文件 | | `~/.dsh/memory-settings.json` | 记忆的全局开关与偏好 | | `~/.dsh/system-prompt/settings.json` | 系统提示词与风格档位 | ## 安装 **推荐：内置插件安装程序。** 打开「设置 → 内置插件」，粘贴包名，点安装，再重启应用： ``` dsh-memory-system-prompt ``` 安装程序会自动写进 `dsh.profile.bundles`，不用手改任何文件。 命令行方式（先完全退出应用）： ```bash cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop pnpm add dsh-memory-system-prompt ``` 然后把包名加进 `dsh.profile.bundles`，重启应用。 ## 注意 - 记忆索引通过 `systemPrompt.context` 注入，不是 `agent.inject`——后者会排队成一条用户消息，导致模型在回答完再自问自答一轮。 - 索引刷新挂在 `agent/created` 和 `turn/start` 上，因为在 assemble 之后才拿得到最新内容。 - 系统提示词部分**不把 `systemPrompt` 写进 `inject`**，而是运行时用 `agent.ctx.get('systemPrompt')` 取。硬注入会让 fiber 在服务未就绪时被挂起，表现是插件静默不加载、设置里一片空白。 --- **English** | [中文](#chinese) Global memory for DeepSeek Harness: the model can write facts into a persistent store and read them back later. The index is injected into the system prompt every turn, **without consuming conversation context**. The package also carries the **user-level system prompt** feature (the former standalone `dsh-system-prompt` is merged in). Both halves share one settings page. ## What it solves Models have no cross-session memory. This plugin provides a persistent, searchable memory area: - **The model writes**: stable facts discovered in conversation (preferences, conventions, environment details) are saved through tools; - **The index is always present**: each turn injects "title + one-line summary" into the system prompt, so the model knows what exists; - **Bodies are on demand**: the full text is read only when needed, so the whole store never floods the context; - **Per-conversation opt-out**: a conversation that should not carry memory can turn it off. ## Tools | Tool | Purpose | |---|---| | `memory_save` | Save or update one memory (same slug overwrites) | | `memory_read` | Read one memory body by slug | | `memory_list` | List memories (index only by default) | | `memory_delete` | Delete one memory | ## User-level system prompt Written once, applied to every conversation; can also be disabled per conversation. - **Custom body**: anything you want to impose on the model long-term (tone, format, prohibitions); - **Nine style dials**: build a behavior instruction from dials instead of prose — base tone, warmth, enthusiasm, emoji, visual answers, headings and lists, quick answers, suggestions, verbosity; - **Two injection positions**: part of the system prompt, or a context fragment. Every dial defaults to "default"; keeping all of them default produces no extra content. ## UI - **Composer toggle (left side)**: three states (off / partial / on), per conversation; - **Settings → Memory & Prompt**: global switch, individual memories, system prompt and style dials, first-run guide. ## Storage | Path | Contents | |---|---| | `~/.dsh/memory/` | One file per memory | | `~/.dsh/memory-settings.json` | Global switch and preferences for memory | | `~/.dsh/system-prompt/settings.json` | System prompt and style dials | ## Install **The built-in plugin installer is the recommended way.** Open Settings → Built-in Plugins, paste the package name, press install, then restart the app: ``` dsh-memory-system-prompt ``` The installer writes the entry into `dsh.profile.bundles` for you; no manual file edits. From the command line (quit the app completely first): ```bash cd ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop pnpm add dsh-memory-system-prompt ``` Add the package name to `dsh.profile.bundles` and restart the app. ## Notes - The memory index is injected through `systemPrompt.context`, not `agent.inject`. The latter queues a user message, which makes the model answer its own question for another turn. - The index refreshes on `agent/created` and `turn/start`, because the content is only current after assembly. - The system-prompt half deliberately does **not** list `systemPrompt` in `inject`; it resolves the service at runtime via `agent.ctx.get('systemPrompt')`. A hard injection parks the fiber while the service is not ready, which shows up as a silently unloaded plugin and an empty settings page.

plugins.description: See which semantic primitives your answer lights up, live — brain-shaped node graph, EEG-style traces, composition card. 语义脉冲 / HowNet 义原可视化
plugins.readme_text:
# 语义脉冲 · dsh-primitive-pulse

在 DSH 里实时看**当前这段回答**点亮了哪些语义基元。右下角一个圆钮，点开是三个面板，也可以切到全屏背景模式。

![面板](assets/screenshots/sfx_panel.png)

**基元星图**——340 个簇铺成立体脑形，被命中的节点变亮，两端都亮的连线更亮：

![基元星图](assets/screenshots/sfx_brain.png)

**基元流 + 指纹卡**——上面是义原沿 token 的激活曲线（脑电样式多导联），下面是按分区聚合的构成表：

![基元流与指纹卡](assets/screenshots/sfx_stream.png)

| 面板 | 看什么 |
| --- | --- |
| 基元星图 | 340 个簇铺成立体脑形：被命中的节点变亮，两端都亮的连线更亮；静息时是一张暗着的网格 |
| 基元流 | 多条多导联，每条是一个义原沿 token 的激活曲线（带衰减拖尾），合成在一张脑电图纸上 |
| 指纹卡 | 义原按分区聚合后的构成表，按占比降序，和样例基线对比 |

**形状是隐喻，不是脑活动。** 面板里没有 fNIRS、没有皮层柱、没有任何神经测量；点亮的依据全部是文本经 HowNet 义原体系分解后的统计。所以页脚写的是「形状是隐喻，不是脑活动」。

## 它到底做了什么

1. 宿主把每轮 assistant 正文交给插件（`session/event` 的 `assistant/message`，不抓屏、不读你的输入）。
2. 正文用内置的中英词表切成词，每个词查 HowNet 义原（2,168 个义原 / 133,759 个中文词 / 48,042 个英文词）。
3. 逐 token 累出「义原激活流」，按指数衰减滚成曲线；同时聚成 340 个簇，投到预生成的三维坐标上。
4. 浏览器端只负责画：一个轮询 `/dsh-pulse/state`，拿到帧自己渲染。

## 装

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:DreamLoomStudio/dsh-primitive-pulse
```

装完**重启 DSH Desktop**（宿主在启动时收集一次注入行，运行期加不进来）。重启后：

- 右下角出现圆钮；点它，或按 `Ctrl+Shift+P` 展开面板；
- 想看服务端是否起来，访问 `http://127.0.0.1:43129/dsh-pulse/ping`，返回 JSON 即正常：

```json
{"ok":true,"plugin":"dsh-primitive-pulse","assets":{"widget":25630,"core":11022,"data":4348808},"seq":0,"hasText":false}
```

## 用

- **圆钮可拖动**，位置会记住。
- 面板头部「背景模式」：把星图铺到整个窗口背景，慢慢自转；再点一次关闭（也会记住）。
- 没有新回答时，面板不会空着——回放结束后会按每个节点的峰值做错相位的呼吸，让你仍能看到这段回答激活了哪些区域。
- 手动粘贴：面板底部「手动粘贴」可以贴任意文本（不用等模型回答）试一段。

## 卸载

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-primitive-pulse
```

然后重启 DSH Desktop。

## 数据从哪来

- **2,168 个义原 / 133,759 个中文词 / 48,042 个英文词**：清华 [OpenHowNet](https://github.com/thunlp/OpenHowNet)（HowNet 语义词典）的义原组合，不取例句、不取词频排名。
- **补录 38 条**：HowNet 里没有的现代术语（微分、梯度、插件、面板、残差…）。
- **340 个簇**：义原共现矩阵 → 谱嵌入 → 递归二分聚类，簇名取质心最近的成员义原。
- **三维位置**：侧视剖面取样 + 半球深度 + 空间近邻网格（1,342 条边）。

词表与坐标全部离线打包在 `assets/sememe-data.js`（4.3 MB），**运行时不联网、不调模型、不上传任何内容**。

## 隐私边界

- 插件只在**服务端内存**里保留**最近一段** assistant 正文（`state.text`），进程退出即消失，不落盘、不写日志。
- 浏览器只向**本机**的 `/dsh-pulse/state` 取数据，路由先过宿主的 `connection.requestRejection` 信任栅栏（拿不到栅栏就 fail-closed）。
- 没有账号，没有统计，没有远程上报。

## 已知限制

- 宿主只推「一整条 assistant 消息」，没有逐字 delta：所以是**回答落地后回放**，不是逐字实时。
- 拿不到 `logprobs`（内核目前不暴露），所以没有「模型犹豫度」这一维。
- 多义词按 HowNet 第一个义项算，偶尔会出笑话（`把` → 把手、`世界` → 天体）。
- 未登录词会显示在底部（`未登录义原 N%`），不影响其余部分。

## 开发

先 clone 仓库（`test/` 与 `script/` 不在发布包的 `files` 里，装进 `node_modules` 的那份没有它们）：

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/DreamLoomStudio/dsh-primitive-pulse.git
cd dsh-primitive-pulse
node test/smoke.mjs            # 核心链路（分词 → 义原流 → 簇帧 → 指纹）
node test/widget_headless.mjs  # 挂件 DOM/Canvas 用最小桩跑一遍
node test/english.mjs          # 英文词表
```

资产同步（如果你在本仓库之外改了 `core.js` / 词表）：`node script/sync-assets.mjs`。

MIT License · 数据来自 OpenHowNet，遵守其原始许可。

plugins.description: Author, inspect, and export editable presentation decks one slide at a time.
plugins.readme_text:
# DeckCraft Use

## Plugin marketplaces

This plugin belongs to **AIGC content creation**.

| Category | Marketplace | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full-stack development | [Full Stack Plugins](https://github.com/partme-ai/full-stack-plugins) | Architecture and UI design, code understanding, quality checks, code review, workflow governance, and server operations |
| AIGC content creation | [Full AIGC Plugins](https://github.com/partme-ai/full-aigc-plugins) | Image, video, audio, music, 3D, and multimodal content creation |

![DeckCraft Use — editable presentations from a coding agent](assets/official-logo.png)

> Author, inspect and export a real presentation from your agent host — one slide at a time, with the editable source deck kept as the deliverable.

[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/release-0.1.0--dev.20261019.1-1A73E8)](https://github.com/full-aigc-plugins/deckcraft-plugin/releases)
[![Skills](https://img.shields.io/badge/skills-10-00A67E)](#skills)
[![MCP tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP%20tools-33-00A67E)](#mcp-tools)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-green)](LICENSE)

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) · [Install](#installation) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Skills](#skills) · [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Positioning

`deckcraft` lets an agent host drive the DeckCraft engine through a bundled stdio MCP server and a set of presentation skills, so a request ends with an editable `.deckcraft` deck plus the exports you asked for. The plugin owns skill routing, the same-session editor bridge and package pinning. It does not replace DeckCraft, its engine, or the host runtime.

| Property | Value |
| :--- | :--- |
| Plugin ID | `deckcraft` |
| Version | `0.1.0-dev.20261018.4` |
| Status | Development preview; production promotion blocked, all-host acceptance open |
| Editor runtime | Node.js 24, started from `ui/bootstrap.mjs` |
| Upstream reference | DeckCraft `0.3.0` (`d0e57d7e25f9852179cc66be12dd6188f1c05535`) |
| Optional CLI | `deckcraft-cli`, if your host already has it on `PATH` |
| License | Apache-2.0 |

## Installation

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 24 on `PATH`; the bundled stdio MCP server runs on it.
- Network access on the first editor launch. The plugin downloads and verifies the pinned editor archive; a complete release ZIP already contains it, so no Rust toolchain and no `npm install` are required.
- A `deckcraft-cli` installation only if you want the native CLI path. The plugin never installs or upgrades it.
- A host that supports plugins or stdio MCP. Embedded panels additionally require MCP Apps or a built-in browser.

### From the plugin marketplace

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add partme-ai/full-aigc-plugins
codex plugin add deckcraft@full-aigc-plugins
```

Restart the host, open a new task, and ask DeckCraft to start a deck.

### Other host manifests

| Host | Manifest | Path base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Standard Agent Plugins 1.0.0 | `plugin.json`, `mcp.json` | `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` |
| Codex | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/mcp.json` | plugin root relative to `cwd` |
| Claude Code | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` |

Kimi (`kimi.plugin.json`), DeepSeek Harness (`dsh/`) and the WorkBuddy example (`hosts/workbuddy/mcp.json`) are also present. `hosts/native-cli/mcp.json` shows the optional `deckcraft-cli mcp` server instead of the bundled editor.

## Quick start

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Install plugin] --> B[Restart and open a task]
    B --> C[open_editor]
    C --> D{editor_status ready?}
    D -->|No| C
    D -->|Yes| E[new_presentation]
    E --> F[add_slide / add_shape / insert_chart]
    F --> G[inspect_slide]
    G --> H[save_presentation / export]
```

1. Open the editor with an explicit `workspace` argument.
2. Start a deck with `new_presentation`, or open an existing one with `open_presentation`.
3. Read `list_commands` before complex edits; command IDs and `enabled` state come from the live registry.
4. After each block of edits, call `inspect_document` or `inspect_slide`, and `render_slide` when you need a picture.
5. Save the `.deckcraft` source, then export. Reopen the source to confirm the slides are still editable.

## What you can build

| Workflow | Built-in path | Verifiable output |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Pitch deck with problem, evidence and ask | `deckcraft-pitch-deck` | Slide-per-message deck with speaker notes |
| Weekly or status report | `deckcraft-weekly-report` | Progress, risk and next-step slides |
| Training courseware | `deckcraft-training-slides` | Explanation, example, exercise and recap slides |
| Data narrative | `deckcraft-data-story` + `insert_chart` | Chart bound to your data with title and labels |
| Brand template reuse | `deckcraft-brand-template` | Master-styled slides, consistent layouts |
| Redesign an existing deck | `deckcraft-slide-redesign` | Restructured deck, original retained |
| Option comparison | `deckcraft-option-comparison` + `insert_table` | Editable comparison table with units and sources |
| Delivery | `save_presentation`, `export` | Editable source plus PPTX, PDF or image output |

## Skills

| Skill | What it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `deckcraft-use` | Main entry: create, modify, inspect or export a deck through the connected MCP or an installed CLI |
| `deckcraft-editor` | Open the real editor in the host and keep agent edits on the same page |
| `deckcraft-pitch-deck` | Problem, solution, evidence and ask for a project pitch |
| `deckcraft-weekly-report` | Progress, issues, metrics and next-week plan |
| `deckcraft-training-slides` | Explanation, examples, exercises and recap |
| `deckcraft-data-story` | Data conclusion and business interpretation, with chart plans |
| `deckcraft-brand-template` | Master style and recurring layouts for a brand |
| `deckcraft-slide-redesign` | Restructure and visually improve an existing deck |
| `deckcraft-option-comparison` | Cost, lead time and risk compared in an editable table |
| `deckcraft-scenario-playbooks` | Step-by-step recipes for metric briefing, comparison, flow, risk matrix, trend, training Q&A and handoff |

Skills come from the independent `deckcraft-skills` source and are pinned by `scenario-candidates.json` with per-skill SHA-256 digests. They carry scenario knowledge and execution contracts, not a second engine.

## MCP tools

One bundled server, `deckcraft-editor`, speaking **stdio**. The local HTTP listener only serves the editor page and its same-session bridge. The catalogue exposes 33 tools: 28 agent-callable tools and 5 `_editor_*` bridge tools the panel uses internally.

| Family | Tools | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Session | `open_editor`, `open_browser_editor`, `editor_status` | Open the editor and confirm that it attached |
| Discovery | `list_commands`, `call_app` | List live commands; `call_app` reaches app-level control methods (desktop app only) |
| Command gateway | `run_command`, `batch` | Run one command, or an ordered batch with explicit failure semantics |
| Deck management | `new_presentation`, `open_presentation`, `save_presentation`, `export` | Create, open, save and export |
| Slides | `add_slide`, `go_to_slide`, `inspect_slide`, `render_slide` | Add, navigate, read and render one slide |
| Content | `add_shape`, `add_text_box`, `set_text`, `insert_picture`, `insert_table`, `insert_chart` | Place and edit the objects a slide is made of |
| Inspection | `inspect_document` | Titles, page count, objects and text of the whole deck |
| Interaction | `select`, `select_tool`, `pointer`, `key`, `type_text`, `screenshot` | Drive the same paths a mouse and keyboard would; `screenshot` captures the whole window and needs the desktop app |

## Configuration

| Setting | Where | Effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `workspace` argument | `open_editor` / `open_browser_editor` | Binds the task folder; paths outside it are refused |
| `CRAFT_EDITOR_UPDATE=off` | stdio MCP `env` | Use the bundled editor only; no download attempt |
| `CRAFT_EDITOR_CACHE_DIR` | Environment | Absolute directory for verified editor archives |
| `CRAFT_WORKSPACE_ROOT` | Host MCP conf

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex — native subagent progress, in-host worker sessions with per-tier presets, and a multimodal bridge that lends the text-only harness vision and image generation.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

# dsh-ai-code-quality

`dsh-ai-code-quality` 是 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件，为 Agent 提供一组类型化的 `cq_*` 工具，用于执行 [ai-code-quality](https://github.com/lkdx0220/ai-code-quality-skill) 的确定性代码质量流程。

插件本身不重新实现检测规则。每次调用都启动 `cq` CLI，并解析其 `--format json` 输出；扫描、聚合、基线、质量门和豁免账本仍由 cq 负责。插件适合需要在 DSH 会话中检查 Python 仓库、比较质量基线或规划修复批次的项目。

> **语言边界：当前版本只支持 Python 仓库的代码质量扫描。** `cq_scan`、`cq_triage`、`cq_gate`、`cq_diff`、`cq_fix_plan` 和 `cq_spec_rebuild` 依赖 Python 目标与 Python 工具链；对 Java、Go、TypeScript 等非 Python 仓库，不会产生完整的代码质量结论，扫描可能因找不到 `.py` 目标而返回空结果。

语言无关的能力仍可使用：`cq_spec_gate`、`cq_waiver` 和 `cq_promote` 只依赖 git 与 Markdown/spec 文本，不要求 Python 源码。多语言 adapter 尚未包含在当前插件版本中。

## Web UI 范围

这是一个 **host 侧工具插件**，不是 Web UI 插件。它可以安装到 DSH Web profile，并在 Web 会话中提供 `cq_*` 工具；但不会注入浏览器脚本、添加设置页、侧栏按钮、主题或其他可视化组件。因此 `package.json` 有 `dsh.bundle` 配置，但没有 `dsh.client` 配置。

## 能力

| 工具 | 用途 | 是否写入项目 |
|---|---|---:|
| `cq_doctor` | 检查 8 个外部工具、解释器和安装来源 | 否 |
| `cq_scan` | 运行完整或选定 adapter 的扫描，返回 run id、工具状态、跳过项和严重度汇总 | 写入 `audits/<run_id>/` |
| `cq_triage` | 按安全、可靠性、可维护性和测试维度归类 findings，并生成修复批次 | 否 |
| `cq_baseline` | 固化一个扫描 run，供后续 diff/gate 使用 | 写入基线 |
| `cq_diff` | 比较 run 与基线，报告 new/fixed/existing/moved/suppressed | 否 |
| `cq_gate` | 执行 blocker/high、复杂度、覆盖率和基线门禁 | 否 |
| `cq_waiver` | 创建带期限、带理由的 spec-drift 豁免 | 写入决策与账本 |
| `cq_spec_gate` | 检查代码变更是否由 spec proposal 声明 | 否 |
| `cq_fix_plan` | 输出分批修复计划；只做 dry-run | 否 |
| `cq_suppress_reapply` | 按稳定签名把已有 suppression 对齐到新 run | 写入 suppression 账本 |
| `cq_spec_rebuild` | 输出 spec 与代码符号的启发式对账线索 | 否 |
| `cq_promote` | 输出可晋升为 constitution 条款的重复决策候选 | 否 |

`cq_scan` 会明确返回每个 adapter 的 `status`，并把缺失工具列为 `skipped`；`cq_gate` 遇到工具不完整时返回 `cannotJudge`，不会把不完整结果当作通过。

## 安全边界

插件工具面不暴露会直接修改代码的操作。`cq fix --apply` 和 `cq spec-rebuild --apply` 必须由用户在 CLI 中显式执行，再重新扫描和过门禁。

插件包含两类有意的写状态操作：创建 baseline、waiver，以及更新 suppression 账本。这些操作都会返回 CLI 结果，并把审计材料落到项目目录，便于复核和回滚。

## 前置条件

- DSH 宿主支持插件的 `defineTool` 和 bundle 配置。
- Node.js ≥ 20。
- 已安装 [ai-code-quality/cq](https://github.com/lkdx0220/ai-code-quality-skill)。
- `cq` 在 PATH 中可执行，或在插件配置的 `command` 字段中提供替代调用方式。
- 代码质量扫描当前只支持 Python 仓库；非 Python 仓库请只使用明确标注为语言无关的 spec 工具。

插件运行时依赖的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 由 DSH 宿主提供，不能用裸 Node 直接加载插件来代替宿主验证。

## 安装与验证

开发版或本地目录可以安装到目标 profile：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /path/to/dsh-ai-code-quality
dsh --profile <profile> --dump-config
```

安装后重启 DSH 宿主，让 profile 重新装配 bundle。首次验证建议按这个顺序进行：

1. 调用 `cq_doctor`，确认 cq 和外部工具状态。
2. 调用 `cq_scan`，确认返回 `runId`、`tools`、`toolsSkipped`、`notes` 和 `summary`。
3. 使用该 `runId` 调用 `cq_triage` 或 `cq_gate`。
4. 需要比较历史结果时，再创建 baseline 并调用 `cq_diff`。

如果宿主提示 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools unavailable`，说明插件被裸 Node 或错误的 DSH profile 加载；应在实际 DSH 宿主和目标 profile 中验证。

## 配置

| 字段 | 默认值 | 说明 |
|---|---:|---|
| `command` | `cq` | cq CLI 调用方式，例如 `cq` 或 `py -3 -m ai_code_quality.cli` |
| `project` | `.` | 工具未单独指定项目时使用的项目路径 |
| `timeoutMs` | `900000` | 单次 CLI 调用超时时间；`0` 表示不设超时 |
| `maxOutputChars` | `60000` | 每次调用捕获的 stdout/stderr 上限 |

工具参数中的 `project` 会覆盖插件级默认值。`cq_scan` 还支持 `scope`、`adapters` 和 `noDeepsec`；其他参数以工具 schema 为准。

## 本地开发与测试

在插件目录运行：

```bash
npm test
```

冒烟测试覆盖工具注册与 disposer、`output.render` 宿主契约、真实 cq 主路径（环境允许时）、缺失 CLI、非法项目路径以及非 JSON 输出。受限环境中如果禁止管道子进程，普通测试会明确报告主路径 `SKIP`；`SMOKE_STRICT=1` 会把未执行主路径视为失败：

```bash
SMOKE_STRICT=1 npm test
```

测试插件文件本身不等于 DSH 宿主验证；提交前仍应在目标 DSH profile 重启后实际调用 `cq_doctor` 和 `cq_scan`。

## 与 cq Skill 的关系

DSH 插件和 [`agent-adapters/dsh/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/lkdx0220/ai-code-quality-skill/tree/main/agent-adapters/dsh) 是同一 cq CLI 的两种接入方式：

- 插件已装配时，Agent 优先使用 `cq_*` 类型化工具，结果结构稳定，适合编排 scan → triage → gate 流程。
- 插件未装配时，DSH Skill 仍可直接调用 cq CLI，能力保持可用。

插件版本和 cq 本体版本分别维护。发布插件时应同时记录兼容的 cq 版本范围，并附上 `npm test` 与真实宿主验证结果。

## 许可证与第三方工具声明

本插件及 `cq` 编排代码以 MIT 许可证发布，完整文本见 [`LICENSE`](LICENSE)。插件不包含下列检测工具的源代码，只在运行时调用用户环境中已安装的工具；它们的版权归各自作者，并分别遵循上游许可证：

| 工具 | 用途 | 许可证 | 上游 |
|---|---|---|---|
| [ruff](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) | lint、格式检查 | MIT | Astral |
| [mypy](https://github.com/python/mypy) | 静态类型检查 | MIT | python/mypy |
| [radon](https://github.com/rubik/radon) | 圈复杂度、可维护性指数 | MIT | rubik/radon |
| [vulture](https://github.com/jendrikseipp/vulture) | 死代码检测 | MIT | jendrikseipp |
| [pytest](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest) / [pytest-cov](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-cov) | 测试执行、覆盖率 | MIT | pytest-dev |
| [import-linter](https://github.com/seddony/import-linter) | 架构依赖契约 | BSD 2-Clause | seddony |
| [DeepSec](https://github.com/Unclecheng-li/DeepSec) | L1/L2 安全扫描 | MIT | Unclecheng-li |

插件自身只负责 DSH 工具注册与 `cq` CLI 调用；底层检测结论由上述工具产生。

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin for Codex reset events, schedules, and source posts, with a composer status popover and the codex_reset agent tool.
plugins.readme_text: English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) # dsh-codex-reset-tracker DeepSeek Harness plugin for Codex reset status. It adds a composer entry with a compact status popover and registers the read-only `codex_reset` agent tool. ## Acknowledgements Reset signals and available translations are provided by [Did Codex Reset](https://didcodexreset.com/zh/). Thank you to its maintainers for collecting and organizing these public reset signals and providing the [read-only API](https://didcodexreset.com/zh/api.html) and [OpenAPI specification](https://didcodexreset.com/openapi/v1/openapi.json). This repository is a DSH integration of that upstream work; the API does not include account-specific quota information. Original reset announcements are from [Tibo Sottiaux (@thsottiaux)](https://x.com/thsottiaux). ## Screenshots | Light theme | Dark theme | |---|---| | | | ## What it shows - The composer entry opens a compact popover with today's reset status, the latest reset time, and the next scheduled time. - The day check uses the browser's local calendar day. Scheduled events do not count as completed resets. If `completedAt` and `effectiveAt` are unavailable or invalid, the summary uses `announcedAt`. - The popover includes the Tibo Sottiaux source post. It shows the Simplified Chinese translation and the English source when both differ. - New schedule announcements and completed reset events show an unread marker. The marker clears when the popover is open in a visible tab. - The client requests `/status` on mount and refreshes every 10 minutes. The agent tool can query status or paginated records. ## Install from source Clone the repository, then add it to a DSH profile: ```sh git clone https://github.com/loshanvren/dsh-codex-reset-tracker.git cd dsh-codex-reset-tracker dsh plugin --profile add . ``` The package is named `dsh-codex-reset` in the DSH loader and package manifest. ## Agent tool `codex_reset` supports: - `action: "status"` — the latest global and Banked reset signals and the next scheduled reset. - `action: "records"` — one page of records, filtered by `kind`, `page`, and `pageSize`. The tool accepts an optional `lang` for record translations. Successful responses are cached for 60 seconds by default. | Config | Default | Purpose | |---|---:|---| | `apiBaseUrl` | `https://didcodexreset.com/openapi/v1` | Public API base URL used by the agent tool | | `cacheTtlSeconds` | `60` | Tool response cache, from 5 to 3600 seconds | | `timeoutMs` | `20000` | Tool call timeout, from 1000 to 120000 milliseconds | Override these values under the plugin row's `config` in `cordis.patch.yml`. The public API documents a shared limit of 60 requests per hour per IP. ## License The MIT License applies to this repository's code only. It does not relicense Did Codex Reset's data or translations, or Tibo Sottiaux's post and profile image.

plugins.description: DSH 插件：播种智谱 Coding Plan 供应商，对话输入区底部显示用量（5 小时 / 周 / MCP 月度配额）。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-zhipu-provider

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）插件：为 Web GUI 接入智谱 Coding Plan（智谱 OpenAI 兼容 coding 端点），并附带用量展示。

## 功能

- **provider 播种**：启动时把 `zhipu-coding-plan` 路由写入 `llm-pi-ai` 用户设置层——与 Models 页「自定义模型 API」卡片同一条写入路径，按 provider 键合并，与其他插件互不覆盖；模型选择器随即出现 `glm-5.3` / `glm-5.3-flash`。
- **用量 pill**：会话选用智谱模型时，输入卡片下方显示用量 pill——摘要为 5 小时窗口 / 每周配额百分比（≥90% 标红），点击弹出面板查看各配额已用 / 总量 / 剩余与重置时间，标题带套餐名。数据取自智谱开放平台。

## 用法

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/youmu129/dsh-zhipu-provider
```

1. 配置凭证：在设置页录入智谱 Console Key，或设置环境变量 `ZHIPU_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY`；
2. 重启 `dsh web`，选用智谱模型即见 pill；未配置凭证时 pill 显示「未配置」并给出指引。

可选设置（覆盖 schema 默认值）：`baseUrl`（默认 `https://open.bigmodel.cn`，国际站用 `https://api.z.ai`）、`usage.pollIntervalMs` / `usage.requestTimeoutMs`（默认 0，关闭自动轮询，以手动刷新为主）。

## 开发

```powershell
pnpm install
pnpm run build
pnpm test
```

> API Key 只存放于 DSH 凭证机制或 `apiKeyEnv` 引用的环境变量，不入库、不写入日志与文档。

plugins.description: dsh-plugin dsh deepseek-harness plugin-manager settings
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugins-in-settings

把 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)（DSH）**侧栏的「插件」收进设置**：
在 **设置 → 插件** 里新增一个 **「插件管理」** 标签页，把官方插件面板的能力搬进来
（浏览官方 / 已装组合包、**添加插件**、开关组合包、开关单个插件行、卸载）。

> 侧栏原有的「插件」入口**保持原样**。本插件是**再加一个入口**，不是把原来那个拆掉 ——
> 任何一边出问题都不会让对方不可用。

## 装好之后长这样

```
设置 → 插件（官方那一页）
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 内置插件                                                  │
│ 查看内置部署的插件列表                                    │
│                                                          │
│  ┌──────────────┬──────────────┐  ← 官方标签页栏         │
│  │ 插件管理      │ 插件列表      │                        │
│  │ ▔▔▔▔▔▔       │              │  ← 本插件新增的标签页   │
│  ├──────────────┴──────────────┴──────────────────────┐ │
│  │ 运行中的改动会即时生效；个别插件需要…      [刷新]    │ │
│  │                                                     │ │
│  │ ┌─ 添加插件 ──────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │
│  │ │ 输入包名、GitHub 地址或本机目录路径。            │ │ │
│  │ │ [dsh-plugin-whale-pet    ] [安装源▾] [安装]      │ │ │
│  │ │ 请确认插件来源可信。插件以你的权限在本机运行。    │ │ │
│  │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │
│  │                                                     │ │
│  │ 官方                                                │ │
│  │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │
│  │ │ dsh-experimental-voice-input    官方  已停用    │ │ │
│  │ │ …                                      [启用]   │ │ │
│  │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │
│  │                                                     │ │
│  │ 已安装                                              │ │
│  │ ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ │
│  │ │ dsh-better-sidebar                已启用        │ │ │
│  │ │ …                        [停用]  [卸载]         │ │ │
│  │ │ ─────────────────────────────────────────────── │ │ │
│  │ │ sidebar（组合包里的插件行）        [停用]       │ │ │
│  │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**与官方面板的关系**：本插件不重写一套安装器。列表、安装、开关、卸载全部走
**官方同一个远程接口**（`remote.pluginManager`）—— 官方怎么装、怎么开、怎么卸，
这里就是同一条路径，不存在"两份实现漂移"的问题。

### 「添加插件」的四步

1. **填规格** —— 包名（`dsh-xxx`）、`github:作者/仓库`、或本机绝对路径。
2. **宿主先读一遍**（`inspect`）—— 不是有效插件包、读不到源、pnpm 会拒绝的写法，
   都会在**开始装之前**把原因显示在输入框下面，规格留着让你改。
3. **真的开装**（`installBundle`）—— 装上后**默认启用**，装完自动刷新列表。
4. **看结局** —— 按宿主回报的 `application` 分四种：
   装好 / 装好但要重启 / 失败（含 pnpm 挡下的构建脚本，可「同意并重试」）/ 取消。

装的过程中**随时可取消**。如果回应在途中丢了（超时、断线），会拿同一个任务 id
向宿主把结果**问回来**；问不到就如实显示「结果不明」，**绝不谎报成功**。

## 30 秒上手

```powershell
# 方块一：下载 / clone 本仓库，然后
.\install.cmd
# 方块二：完全退出并重开 DSH Desktop（关窗口不够，要退出进程）
# 方块三：设置 → 插件 → 顶部「插件管理」
```

## 安装（三条路，任选）

### 1. 设置面板安装（推荐）

**设置 → 插件 → 添加插件**，填三者之一：

- **本地目录路径**（本仓库解压后那一层目录）
- **`github:Alail691/dsh-plugins-in-settings`**
- **npm 包名**（发布到 registry 后可用）

### 2. 命令行（**只有非 desktop profile 能这么装**）

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile tui add link:"<本插件的绝对路径>"
dsh plugin --profile tui add github:Alail691/dsh-plugins-in-settings
```

> `desktop` 是 Electron 应用保留的 profile，命令行会被直接拒绝：
> `error: profile "desktop" is managed exclusively by the Electron application`。

### 3. 脚本（desktop profile，或设置里没有「插件」面板时）

```powershell
.\install.cmd                    # 装进 desktop
.\install.cmd -Profile tui       # 装进别的 profile
.\install.cmd -WhatIf            # 只看要做什么，不落盘
.\install.cmd -Uninstall         # 卸载
```

脚本做四件事：备份 profile 的 `package.json` → 加一条 `link:` 依赖 →
把包名追加进 `dsh.profile.bundles` → 在 profile 的 `node_modules` 下建链接
（Windows 用 junction，其它平台用符号链接），最后校验这三项都成立。

> **卸载**用面板，或 `install.cmd -Uninstall`。
> 手工建过 junction 的用 `cmd /c rmdir <junction>` ——
> **不要**用 `Remove-Item -Recurse`，那可能顺着链接把插件目录里的文件删掉。

## 它怎么工作

| 半边 | 干什么 |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js`（宿主） | 空逻辑 + 一次客户端产物静态核对。存在的唯一理由是让本包成为 cordis 树上的一行，否则 `dsh.client` 的 bundle 不会被扫进启动图 |
| `lib/client.js`（客户端） | 一个标签页：注册进 `settings.plugins.tab`，用 `remote.pluginManager` 驱动列表 / 开关 / 卸载 |

### 挂在哪儿，为什么

官方 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-settings-plugins` 已经占住了 `settings.section` 里
id 为 `plugins` 的设置页（侧栏文案「内置插件」），并声明了子槽 **`settings.plugins.tab`**
（`list`，scope `root`）用来放"这个页里的各个标签页"；官方自己的只读清单
（`ui-settings-plugin-inventory`）就以 id `all`、order 10 挂在里面。

所以"把插件综合到设置里"最自然、事后最不容易坏的落点就是这里：

- **复用**官方已经建好的设置导航与标签页外壳，只贡献一个标签页；
- **不**新开设置页（会和官方页重复）；
- **不**改官方任何 DOM，**不**抢官方注册（本插件 id 是 `manage`，order 5，排在官方清单前面）；
- **不**动侧栏。

### 数据路径（只用官方公开面）

| 用途 | 接口 |
|---|---|
| 列出组合包 | `ctx.remote.pluginManager.listBundles()` |
| **安装前预检** | `ctx.remote.pluginManager.inspect(spec, { registry }, signal)` |
| **安装** | `ctx.remote.pluginManager.installBundle(spec, { enabled, requestId, registry, approvedBuilds? })` |
| **找回安装结果** | `ctx.remote.pluginManager.waitForInstall(requestId)` |
| **取消安装** | `ctx.remote.pluginManager.cancelInstall(requestId)` |
| 开关组合包 | `ctx.remote.pluginManager.setBundleEnabled(name, enabled)` |
| 开关单个插件行 | `ctx.remote.pluginManager.setPluginEnabled(entryId, enabled)` |
| 卸载 | `ctx.remote.pluginManager.removeBundle(name)` |

安装是一条**四方法链**：`inspect` 先问"这个规格能不能装"，
`installBundle` 带一个**自己生成的 `requestId`** 真开装，
回应丢了就拿同一个 id 走 `waitForInstall` 把结果问回来，
中途取消则走 `cancelInstall`（它可能回 `too-late`，意思是已经装完了）。

`remote.pluginManager` 由官方 `ui-plugin-manager` 的宿主半边暴露。本插件**软探测**它
（`ctx.get("remote")`）而**不是**写成硬依赖 `inject` ——
申明一个可能不存在的服务会让 fiber 停在 PENDING，从而拖累整棵插件树。
探测不到时，标签页显示一条可读的「暂不可用」说明，**其余一切照常**。

## 稳健性

- **fail-open**：远程命名空间缺失 / 方法不全 / 列表读失败 / 任何一步认不出 ——
  都收敛成一条可读文字或一个空列表，**绝不抛**，也绝不影响设置面板、官方插件页与侧栏入口。
- **绝不谎报成功**：安装结局按 `application` 判定；认不出的取值一律算「结果不明」，
  而不是当成成功。回应丢失时先问宿主要结果，问不到就如实说不知道。
- **旧宿主自动降级**：只有管理方法、没有安装方法的宿主上，「安装」按钮**禁用**，
  其余功能照常 —— 不会因为缺一个方法就整页不可用。
- **刷新失败保留旧列表**（与官方面板同样的节奏），只在下面追加一行错误。
- **卸载要按两次**（第一次变成「确定卸载」，失焦即还原），避免误点。
- **安装全程可取消**，且取消后不留下"半装"的假状态。
- **零第三方依赖**：只 `require` 平台种子表里的 `react` / `react/jsx-runtime`，
  无构建步骤 —— `lib/client.js` 就是发布产物（手写、可读）。
- 所有失败路径都有离线断言守着（见下）。

## 开发

```powershell
npm test              # 插件断言（154 项）+ 推送助手决策逻辑（15 项）
npm run preflight     # 对着**真实安装**的官方产物核对契约（35 项）
npm run publish:check # 发布自检（22 项）：占位符 / private / files 白名单 / 产物一致性
npm run verify        # 全部一起跑

npm run test:plugin   # 只跑插件断言
npm run test:push     # 只跑推送助手逻辑（用假 git / 假 GitHub API，不联网）
```

**发布到 GitHub**（面向仓库作者）：

```powershell
npm run push:check    # 先只检查：分支、工作区、仓库是否存在、有没有 dsh-plugin topic
npm run push          # 接远程 + 推 main + 打 tag
```

详见 [`docs/PUBLISHING.md`](docs/PUBLISHING.md) 与 [`docs/GITHUB-SETUP.md`](docs/GITHUB-SETUP.md)。

- `test/run.mjs` 验的是"我们自己的形状对不对"：产物契约、纯函数归一化、
  注册契约、数据路径的成功与失败两条路。
- `test/preflight.mjs` 验的是"我们挂的那个地方还在不在"：直接读官方
  `ui-settings-plugins` / `ui-settings-plugin-inventory` / `ui-plugin-manager`
  的产物（从 profile 的 `node_modules` 或 `app.asar` 里找），核对槽位名、
  注册形状、官方占用的 id，以及安装链路的四个方法名与四种结局取值。
  **官方升级改掉这些时先在这里炸**，而不是等装进真机才发现"设置里是空的"。
- `test/publish-check.mjs` 验的是"**这个包本身够不够格被发布**"：占位符有没有替换、
  有没有误加 `private`、`files` 白名单里的文件是否都在、宿主半边的核对标志
  与产物是否一致。发之前跑一次，全绿再推。
- `test/push-logic.test.mjs` 验的是**推送助手的决策逻辑**：用假的 git 与假的
  GitHub API，把七种状态（没有 origin / 仓库不存在 / 缺 topic / 工作区脏 /
  非 main 分支 / origin 指向别处 / 全绿）各跑一遍，断言它**该继续时继续、
  该拦住时拦住**。不联网、不碰真仓库。
  这是一份**回归测试** —— 它曾经在"还没有 origin"（首次推送的常态）
  这个最容易崩、也最该帮上忙的状态下直接抛堆栈。

本机没有可离线使用的真 React（`app.asar` 里不带），所以渲染层是
`test/harness.mjs` 里的**保状态 React 桩**（`useState` / `useMemo` / `useCallback` /
`useEffect` / `useId`，含 setState 触发的重渲染）；数据路径与注册路径跑的都是真代码。

## 兼容性

- 依赖官方**语义契约**：槽位名 `settings.plugins.tab`、远程命名空间 `remote.pluginManager`
  及其方法名。官方若改这些，本插件会**静默退回"暂不可用"**（fail-open），
  不会把官方界面改坏；`npm run preflight` 会先一步报出来。
- 需要**完全重启** DSH Desktop 才生效（客户端 bundle 在启动时注入）。
- 本插件**不注册任何宿主钩子、不注入会话消息、不监听 agent 事件** ——
  结构上只碰一个 UI 槽位与几个远端管理方法。

## 已知限制

- 官方 `listBundles()` 的回应形状由宿主决定，本插件按已观察到的字段
  （`official` / `installed`，以及平铺数组与 `{bundles:[]}` 两种退路）取值；
  认不出就显示空列表而不是猜测。
- **安装源**用的是宿主 `registries()` 给的列表 + 一个「默认安装源」。
  官方面板还会在首次使用时**并行探测** npm 官方源与 npmmirror、把选择记进
  `localStorage`，并在 GitHub 连不上时主动提示改用镜像 —— 这些**本插件没做**。
  安装源默认交给 pnpm 自己的配置，需要换源时在下拉里手动选。
- **不显示 pnpm 的实时输出**。官方面板会把 pnpm 的命令行与输出折在
  「显示安装详情」里；本插件只报最终结局与失败原因。
- 安装时**一律带上 `enabled: true`**（装完即启用）。官方面板是先装上、
  再让你自己决定要不要现在启用。

这三条是有意的取舍：把管理做扎实，把"长尾的安装体验"留给官方面板
（侧栏入口仍在原处）。要哪一条补上，提 issue 即可。

plugins.description: A portable memory protocol for AI agents — load it as standing rules; a curation discipline + reference spec + optional cap hook.
plugins.readme_text:
**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

# Engramory

[![CI](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/tinqiao-oss/engramory/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Python 3.9+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.9%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)

**An opinionated, zero-infrastructure memory *protocol* for small-scale, local,
file-based agent memory** — a strict curation discipline plus a validator
(`tools/engramory_doctor.py`), loaded as **standing rules** (`CLAUDE.md` /
`AGENTS.md` / your host's rules file). It is not a database, a framework, or a
relevance-loaded skill. Memory is a folder of small, human-readable markdown files
plus one always-loaded index. No database, no embeddings, no server — just
plain-text files you can open, read, edit, and diff in any editor (the live store
itself stays git-ignored).

> *Engramory* — coined from *engram* (the physical trace a memory leaves in the
> brain) + *memory*. Here: one file = one fact.

> ⚠️ **Unrelated projects share this name.** *engram + memory* is an obvious
> coinage and at least one other repository arrived at it independently. This
> project is only ever `tinqiao-oss/engramory` (npm: `dsh-engramory`); a same-named
> repo under a different owner is not a fork, a mirror, or a newer version of it.

> 🤖 **Are you an AI agent, asked to install or check this?** Start at
> **[AGENT-SETUP.md](AGENT-SETUP.md)**, not at the install steps below. It is the
> procedure for working out what your host can actually enforce, whether a store
> already exists, what you must not touch, and what to tell the user — the parts
> agents reliably get wrong when improvising.

> **Status: 0.12.1 — experimental.** The hard index cap (a `PreToolUse` hook) is
> deterministic for the matched direct-edit tools (`Edit | Write | MultiEdit`) but
> NOT a global write guard (shell tools — Bash, PowerShell, a background Monitor
> command — plus MCP file tools, external editors, and sync clients bypass it);
> the discipline loads as standing rules the model follows, so it's
> best-effort, not guaranteed on every task (see [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) §8). Assumes a
> single writer / serialized writes. Don't rely on it as a "mandatory, reliable,
> cross-agent" memory layer yet.

---

## What this is — and is NOT

Engramory is **not a new memory architecture**. The "markdown files + a small index
loaded into context + the model curates it" pattern is now the mainstream shape
for agent memory, and it ships in several places already. Engramory stands on:

- **Claude Code native auto-memory** — the same markdown-`MEMORY.md`-index +
  lazy detail-file pattern; its system prompt even uses the same
  `user | feedback | project | reference` type vocabulary (per
  [anthropics/claude-code#58840](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/58840);
  the *public docs* describe only the index + topic files). Engramory is a
  disciplined superset of this default.
- **[basic-memory](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory)** — markdown
  source-of-truth, YAML frontmatter `type`, `[[wikilink]]` graph, local-first.
- **[obsidian-second-brain](https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain)**,
  **[claude-memory-compiler](https://github.com/coleam00/claude-memory-compiler)**
  ("a loaded index beats vector search at personal scale"), and the broader family
  of markdown-memory skills.

What Engramory contributes is the **opinionated bundle + the discipline**, not the
primitives. Do not claim novelty on markdown, frontmatter, wikilinks, a loaded
index, one-file-per-fact notes, or curation hygiene — all are prior art.

## What's actually differentiated

1. **A role/purpose ontology, headed by `feedback` = procedural memory.** The
   semantic / episodic / **procedural** split is established prior art — the CoALA
   taxonomy, and a named procedural type in LangMem and mem0 — so Engramory does not
   claim the category. What it does is make procedural `feedback` the *spine* of a
   deliberately tiny, hand-authored, human-readable set, with required **Why:** /
   **How to apply:** lines, instead of auto-extracting it into a vector/graph store.
   The contribution is the packaging and discipline, not the ontology.

2. **The curation contract as concrete behaviour** the protocol applies (model-followed, not a hard gate): dedup-before-write,
   update-don't-duplicate, delete-when-wrong, and a negative-scope rule ("don't
   store what git/CLAUDE.md/the code already records"). Surveys consistently name
   *modify/delete/forget* as the most under-implemented memory operation — Engramory
   makes it the spine.

3. **A bounded index designed not to silently rot.** The index loads every session and
   Claude Code reads the first 200 lines / 25 KB (documented behavior), so an unbounded index silently
   drops memories off the end. Engramory warns at 150 lines / 20 KB, compacts-or-asks
   before 200 / 25 KB, and ships a hard `PreToolUse` hook backstop (it blocks only
   *growth* past the cap — shrinking/compaction edits always pass). Both the line and
   byte caps apply — whichever is hit first triggers (an index can be under the line
   count yet over on bytes when the lines run long).

   Claude Code has since followed up on this natively: v2.1.186 (released
   2026-06-22) reminds the agent to compact the index when it nears the cap, and
   v2.1.210 (released 2026-07-14) turned an over-cap write into an explicit error
   instead of a silent truncation. Both are after-the-fact alerts, though — the
   write still lands, and entries past the cap stay invisible until someone
   compacts. Engramory's hook denies the write *before* it happens, so a write
   through the matched edit tools never leaves the index over-cap in the first
   place (writes outside them — a shell, an MCP file tool — are not gated; see the
   status note above and SKILL.md §8). The native alerts validate the direction
   and make a welcome second layer — and older versions and other hosts still
   have neither.

## How it compares

| | storage | recall | human-readable | typed ontology | curation discipline | bounded index | infra |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Engramory** | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ role-based (4) | ✅ contract (model-run) | ✅ 150/200 + hook | none |
| CC auto-memory | md files | loaded index → open file | ✅ | ✅ same 4 types | partial (auto) | ~200-line window* | none (built-in) |
| basic-memory | md + SQLite | semantic/FTS search | ✅ | ✅ freeform type | schema + overwrite checks | ❌ (no loaded index) | SQLite + embeddings |
| obsidian-second-brain | md vault | index-first + search | ✅ | folder-typed | ✅ reconcile/lint | partial | none |
| mem0 / Zep | vector/graph DB | semantic | ❌ (DB) | typed (prefs/episodic/proc.; Zep custom) | auto-extract | n/a | DB + embeddings |
| [agentmemory](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory) | SQLite + vector index (+opt. graph) | hybrid BM25+vector (+opt. graph), RRF | ❌ (DB/engine) | ✅ 4-tier lifecycle (work./epis./sem./proc.) | auto (capture + dedup + decay) | n/a | iii engine (local) + opt. embeddings |

Engramory's lane: **minimalism + actionable role typing + curation discipline, zero
infra.** It does *not* try to out-search basic-memory, out-scale mem0, or
out-capture agentmemory — those solve a different problem (auto-capture /
auto-ingest at volume) at a different cost point. agentmemory is the closest
heavyweight foil: also local-first, but it bets on automatic capture (lifecycle
hooks) + hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vectors + optional graph) on a SQLite/`iii`
engine, where Engramory bets on hand-curation + a tiny always-loaded index and
ships no engine at all.

\* Claude Code's [memory docs](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/memory)
document this exactly: *"the first 200 lines of `MEMORY.md`, or the first 25KB,
whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation."* Other hosts
vary, so the window stays configurable via the hook's env vars.

## Where it fits — and the goal

Engramory is a **portable memory *discipline*, not a

plugins.readme_text:
dsh-pr-inbox

侧边栏里的 GitHub PR 收件箱：我提的 / 待我审 / 我合并的 三桶照进 DSH 侧栏， 一眼看完"该我动手的那几件"。绑定当前会话工作区的仓库，复用本机已登录的 gh，插件不存任何凭据，只读。

## 为什么需要它 "有没有该我动的 PR" 是个**每隔十几分钟就会重新出现**的问题。现在的做法通常是： 切到浏览器 → 打开 GitHub → 在 Notifications 和几个仓库的 Pull requests 页之间来回看 → 还得自己记住哪些仓库跟自己有关。GH 的通知（网页/邮件/桌面）又是全站级别的噪音： 推送、issue、CI 失败混在一起，真正"等我 review"的那两三条淹没在里面。 这个插件把这件事挪回你**正在用的地方**： - **绑定工作区**：不用选仓库——会话在哪个仓库，面板就是哪个仓库的 PR（`upstream` 优先、其次 `origin`，再退到第一个 remote；fork 布局会绑到主仓而不是你的 fork）。 - **三桶就是三个动作语义**：`我提的`（我该跟进）、`待我审`（等我的动作，计数会变色）、 `我合并的`（我刚做的事落地没有）。想扫的时候一屏扫完。 - **点开就是全文**：正文、评论与评审摘要、改动文件清单都在面板里渲染，读 PR 描述与 讨论不用跳浏览器（看 diff / 行内 review 评论仍要 GitHub，见「已知限制」）。 - **零新凭据**：只用你**已经登录**的 `gh`。不申请 token、不填 PAT、不落盘。 与相邻方案的区别：GitHub 通知是**全站推送**（且不止 PR）；编辑器里的 GitHub 插件通常 绑在"当前文件/当前 diff"。这里是"**当前工作区 + 与我相关**"这一刀，代价是必须先装 `gh` 并登录（见下）。 ## 安装 前置：DSH 已装、本机 `gh` 已登录（`gh auth login`）。面板页签挂在 [better-sidebar](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar) 上，所以它也要装。 **dsh 0.2.1 线需要 better-sidebar ≥ 0.28.0**：0.26.x 的 `inject` 仍要求 0.2.1 已移除的 `webRuntime`，页签会永久 pending、界面上没有任何入口。 > **当前状态：已发布到公开仓库 `omdsh-dev/dsh-pr-inbox`**（2026-10-17）。用下面的 > git 源安装；`lib/` 已随仓库提交，不需要构建授权。 **① 装页签宿主**（两种方式都要） ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-better-sidebar ``` **② 装本插件** ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add "github:omdsh-dev/dsh-pr-inbox" # 钉版本：用 ...#v0.1.1 ``` 本地开发/自测也可以走 tarball（需要 clone 仓库）： ```bash pnpm install && pnpm pack # 产出 dsh-pr-inbox-0.1.1.tgz dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-pr-inbox-0.1.1.tgz ``` 装完刷新页面（或按 DSH 提示重启 web）即可在**右侧栏**看到 `PR` 页签： 展开右栏 → 从页签列表里选 `PR`。 > `lib/` 构建产物随仓库提交，所以 git 源安装**不需要**任何构建授权 > （不会让你放行 `allowBuilds`，也不会在你的机器上跑构建脚本）。 ## 用起来是什么样 | | | |---|---| | **顶部** | 搜索框（标题 / 编号 / 作者 / 标签，只在已加载的行里过滤）+ `简洁/详细` 切换（选择会记住）+ 刷新 | | **简洁档** | 单行 28px：行首头像 · `#编号` · 标题 · 时间；适合快速扫 | | **详细档** | 两行 50px：第一行与简洁档**同一个位置**，第二行补作者、合并时间、标签、评论数 | | **分区块** | 三个桶各自成区，滚动时当前区的名字与计数贴在上沿；点击区头折叠。空桶只留一行计数（不显示占位文案）；只加载了一页时计数显示 `已加载 / 总数` | | **点开一行** | 面板内打开完整 PR：正文（markdown 渲染，图片走宿主代理）、评论与评审摘要、改动文件清单（状态色标 + 增删行数）；`返回列表` 会回到原来的滚动位置与行焦点，当前项有强调条；详情里按 Esc 也能返回 | | **状态行** | 底部常显绑定的仓库、当前 gh 账号与数据的读取时间（详情页也在） |

> 截图只截插件面板本身（不含宿主聊天区）；详情预览用一篇纯文字正文的 PR，避免把正文里的大图当成插件界面。 ## 能力面 | 面 | 说明 | |---|---| | 侧边栏页签 | `PR` 页签，挂在 better-sidebar 的右栏；跟随 DSH 语言（中/英）与深浅主题 | | 三桶列表 | `我提的`（`author:@me`，开着的）、`待我审`（`review-requested:@me`）、`我合并的`（`is:merged author:@me`，最近 20 条，按合并时间倒序展示） | | 行内操作 | 点行开详情；行内 `↗` 在 GitHub 打开（悬停/键盘聚焦才现形）；点击穿透不会误开外链 | | PR 详情 | 正文、评论与评审摘要（APPROVED / CHANGES_REQUESTED 等）、改动文件清单、分支与增删行、合并/更新时间；正文与单条评论有上限并**如实标注截断** | | 图片 | 正文与评论里的图片都会渲染：GitHub 编辑器插入的 `` HTML 形态会被改写成 markdown 图片，仓库内**相对路径**图片经插件自有路由代理取字节（受限网络下 `raw.githubusercontent.com` 不可达；同时也覆盖私有仓库） | | 头像 | 作者头像；CDN 不可达时回退成首字母圆底——**不会出现破图图标** | | 语言 | 界面文案随 DSH 语言（zh / en）；插件在 Plugins 页的标题与描述也有中英两份 | ## 环境与前置 - **本机 `gh` 必须已登录**：面板的数据全部来自 `gh`（列表走 `gh api search/issues`，详情走 `gh api`）。缺 `gh` 或未登录时，面板给的是可操作提示（装 gh / `gh auth login`）， 而不是空白列表。 - **只支持 `github.com`**：其它 host（自建 GitLab / Gitea 等）会在列表里留一句说明， 详情返回 `unsupported-host`。 - **需要 better-sidebar**：页签宿主。没装时 host 半照常工作，但界面上没有入口 （这是有意设计：不静默失败，也不假装能用）。 ## 已知限制 - **只读**：没有任何写操作——不评论、不 approve、不 merge，也不接管聊天里的 GitHub 链接。 - **`我合并的` 是最近 20 条**，不是时间窗；取数按 GitHub 搜索的 updated 取一页，展示时再按 合并时间倒序。**搜索只在已加载的行里做**，不会去 GitHub 全量搜。 - **详情不含 diff、行内 review 评论与 CI/checks**：review 只到 review 摘要；要读某条行内意见 或看改动本身，仍要打开 GitHub。 - **`gh` 的速率与超时**会如实反映在面板上（未登录 / 限流 / 超时各有各的提示与错误码）。 - **正文图片**只走"仓库内相对路径 + 公开/私有仓库的 `refs/pull//head`"；正文里的 外链图片直接由浏览器加载（受限网络下可能显示不出来）。 - 面板读的是**当前工作区**：会话还没确定工作目录时，面板会提示先产生一次工具调用 或打开文件，让它绑定到某个仓库。 ## 兼容性 | dsh 版本 | 状态 | |---|---| | `0.2.1-rc.1` + better-sidebar `0.28.0` | ✅ 已验证（2026-10-17）：13 个门全绿（静态 9 + git 源 / mounted 浅色+深色 / negative-control / standalone） | | `0.2.0-rc.2` + better-sidebar `0.26.x` | ✅ 已验证（2026-10-16）：真实实例里装、跑、点开详情，含 git 源安装与负控 | | 其它版本 | ⚠️ 未验证。升级 dsh 后若**右栏没有 `PR` 页签**或**面板一直空白**，多半是宿主服务名/槽名或 client 契约变了；0.2.1 线先确认 better-sidebar ≥ `0.28.0` | ## 插件管理 装/卸/启停用官方 CLI：`dsh plugin --profile web add|remove <包>`；已装插件在**侧边栏 Plugins 页**里查看与配置——每个插件自己的配置页挂在那个包页上（Settings 里的「插件」 只是只读清单，改不了配置）。 ## 开发与验证 ```bash pnpm install && pnpm build # 改源码后必须重建并提交 lib/（CI 会校验无漂移） node scripts/gates/run.mjs # 静态门：包契约 / 发布卫生 / 决策记录 / 文档链接 / 产物新鲜度 / 单测 node scripts/gates/run.mjs --list # 还有哪些实例门（真装真跑、负控、git 源安装冒烟） ``` 工程备忘录（机制、实测环境事实、验证证据、决策记录索引）在 [docs/engineering-notes.md](docs/engineering-notes.md)。 ## 许可 MIT

plugins.description: Noema long-term memory plugin for DSH: durable, inspectable agent memory with recall tools and a settings page.
plugins.readme_text:
DSH Noema

Long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness — durable, inspectable agent memory backed by Noema.
Recall Before Work • Import From 9 Agent Tools • Settings-Page Memory Management • Crash Keep-Alive • Hot Reload

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-noema · Tested with DSH 0.2.0-rc.2

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The Noema Memory settings page — import sources, memory management, and live server status

## Why DSH Noema DSH Noema connects [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) with [Noema](https://github.com/ZSeven-W/noema) — a local-first, non-vector memory system for coding agents — so an Agent keeps durable knowledge across sessions instead of starting every conversation from zero.
### 🧠 Durable Recall Memories persist as inspectable Markdown files under `NOEMA_ROOT` (default `~/.agent-memory/`). `noema_recall` loads relevant context at the start of a session; `noema_search`, `noema_browse`, `noema_catalog`, and `noema_recall_graph` cover lookup, exploration, and auditing. ### 📥 Import From Other Tools `noema_import` reads the memory files of ten other AI coding tools — Codex, Claude Code, opencode, Cursor, Grok, WorkBuddy, Antigravity, Trae, Qoder, Hermes — splits them into sections, and saves each as a durable memory. A content-keyed ledger deduplicates across runs and across tools that share files.
### 🛠️ Settings-Page Management The Noema Memory settings page configures the server command, memory root, budgets, idle/call timeouts, and the guidance section — and a Manage memories card searches, browses, adds, reviews, and deletes stored memories directly. ### 🩺 Keep-Alive The memory server stays up: idle timeout defaults to never, and a keep-alive loop restarts the `noema-mcp` child in the background when it crashes or exits, with a configurable check interval and restart backoff.
### 🔍 Smart Entity Extraction Noema's extraction engine combines jieba word segmentation with high-precision signals — English proper nouns, CJK names and technical terms, quoted topics, and repetition — with stopword and path filters, so the PageIndex topic catalog stays clean. ### ⚡ Hot Reload After the first boot, the plugin never needs a restart again: `pnpm run build` hot-reloads the host plugin through Cordis HMR, and `ppnpm run build:client` hot-swaps the browser bundle over the client-hmr SSE channel.
## Install into DSH ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-noema@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-noema dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately and Cordis HMR can watch the compiled output. The plugin bundles the `noema-mcp` binary through per-platform optional npm packages. To build it yourself instead, run `cargo build --release -p noema-mcp` inside the bundled `noema` submodule, or point the Server command setting at any `noema-mcp` build. ## Memory Tools The model-facing tools mirror the Noema MCP surface: | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `noema_recall` | Recall relevant memories for a query, with a token budget. | | `noema_search` | Full-text search over stored memories. | | `noema_browse` | Browse the PageIndex catalog for a topic or entity. | | `noema_catalog` | Render the full memory catalog as markdown. | | `noema_recall_graph` | Multi-hop recall through links and shared entities. | | `noema_neighbors` | One graph hop from a memory. | | `noema_explain` | Explain why a memory was or was not recalled. | | `noema_remember` | Save a durable fact, decision, constraint, or preference. | | `noema_review_list` | List pending review candidates. | | `noema_review_decide` | Accept, reject, edit, or merge a candidate. | | `noema_forget` | Tombstone or hard-delete a memory. | | `noema_policy_get` / `noema_policy_set` | Read or update the write policy. | | `noema_status` | Server and tenant status: counts, index health, storage root. | | `noema_import` | Import memories from other AI coding tools. | Each tool returns a uniform envelope `{ ok, tool, text }` where `text` carries the full server output. ## Import memories from other tools | Source id | Global files | Workspace files | | --- | --- | --- | | `codex` | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` + the Codex memory pipeline: `~/.codex/memories/MEMORY.md`, `memory_summary.md`, `rollout_summaries/*.md`, `extensions/ad_hoc/notes/*.md` (`raw_memories.md` skipped — it is the uncurated feed) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` | | `claude-code` | `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/CLAUDE.local.md`, `~/.claude/MEMORY.md` | `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `MEMORY.md` | | `opencode` | `~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md` | | `cursor` | `~/.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `~/.cursorrules` | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`, `.cursorrules` | | `grok` | `~/.grok/AGENTS.md` + the Grok cross-session memory: `~/.grok/memory/MEMORY.md`, per-project `MEMORY.md`, and `sessions/*.md` summaries | `AGENTS.md` | | `workbuddy` | `~/.codebuddy/CODEBUDDY.md` (WorkBuddy memory file), `~/.workbuddy/AGENTS.md`, `~/.workbuddy/memory.md`, `~/.config/workbuddy/AGENTS.md`, `~/Library/Application Support/WorkBuddy/AGENTS.md` | `AGENTS.md`, `CODEBUDDY.md` | | `antigravity` | `~/.antigravity/AGENTS.md`, `~/.config/antigravity/AGENTS.md`, `~/Library/Application Support/Antigravity/AGENTS.md` (best-effort; no documented global memory store yet) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md` | | `trae` | `~/.trae/AGENTS.md`, `~/.trae/memory/`, `~/.trae/rules/` (plus the `~/.trae-cn` variants) | `AGENTS.md`, `.trae/rules/` | | `qoder` | `~/.qoder-cn/AGENTS.md`, `~/.qoder-cn/rules/`, the auto-memory roots `~/.qoder-cn/memory/` and `~/.qoder-cn/projects/*/memory/` (plus `~/.qoder` variants) | `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.local.md`, `.qoder/rules/` | | `hermes` | `~/.hermes/memories/` (`MEMORY.md` + `USER.md`) and the global `~/.hermes/SOUL.md` | `.hermes.md`, `HERMES.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | - The `source` argument selects one tool, or omit it to run every source enabled in settings. - The `path` argument selects the workspace root for project-scoped files (defaults to the session workspace; workspace files only load when the Import workspace files setting is on). - Imports are deduplicated through a ledger at `$DSH_HOME/storages/dsh-noema-imports.json`, keyed by file path +

plugins.description: Read-only Agent Team console for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI: live roster, shared task board, and collaboration activity.
plugins.readme_text:
# Agent Team Console

Read-only Agent Teams dashboard for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI (`dsh-agent-team-console`): a
project-scoped, card-grid view of every team, with a top-down pixel-art agent flow graph and rounds /
token / working-time statistics in one first-class main panel.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Repository: <https://github.com/kkomia/dsh-agent-team-console>

> **Unofficial community plugin.** This repository is not part of the DeepSeek official packages, is
> not published or endorsed by DeepSeek, and is not a replacement for the official experimental
> Agent Teams bundle. It is a read-only viewer: it never creates, changes, or completes a team
> member or a task.

## Why this plugin

The official experimental Agent Teams Web UI (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-client-ui-agent-team`)
adds a compact roster and task-board action to the conversation header. That is convenient for a
quick check while you are inside the Lead conversation, but it is not a page of its own.

Agent Team Console keeps the same read-only contract and adds a sidebar entry plus a full main
panel for people who keep a team running for a long stretch:

- A project filter and a compact status strip covering in-progress tasks, running members, token
  usage, blocked tasks, and pending tasks.
- A responsive grid of workspace cards, with at most one team expanded at a time to show the full
  detail.
- A top-down pixel-art agent flow graph: Lead at the top, teammates in balanced rows below,
  downward hand-off links and curved message arcs between them.
- A one-line task summary with in-progress rows on demand, so the page stays visual instead of a wall
  of text.

It is a plain DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web plugin: no build step for users, no npm dependencies, and no
external services.

## Features

- **Sidebar entry and main panel.** A sidebar item labelled "Team console" (the Chinese UI shows
  "团队看板") opens a dedicated page in the main area.
- **Project filter.** When more than one project (workspace) has live teams, a select appears in the
  header. It defaults to "All projects" and narrows the status strip and the team list to one project;
  the choice is client-side and is not persisted.
- **In-progress-first status strip.** A single compact row of five chips: in-progress tasks, running
  members (running / total), token usage for the current selection, blocked tasks (pending tasks that
  are not ready), and pending tasks. Zero values stay visible but muted.
- **Workspace card grid.** Teams are ordered active first, then by most recent activity, and laid out
  as a responsive grid of block cards. A collapsed card shows a status dot, the workspace/project name
  (falling back to "No project", "未分组" in the Chinese UI), an in-progress badge when non-zero, the
  Lead name, a working-vs-idle donut with team rounds and token totals, and a muted work-vs-idle
  caption. At most one team expands at a time: its card spans the full grid row and shows the full
  header, the flow graph, and the task summary. The default expanded card is the first active team; an
  explicit collapse sticks across polls.
- **Top-down flow graph.** The graph is an SVG data-flow diagram: the Lead/root sits at the top centre,
  and teammates sit in balanced rows below — a single row for up to 5 teammates, otherwise two
  balanced rows with the larger row first (up to 8 members, then a "+N" overflow node in the last row).
  Lead-to-teammate hand-off edges are curved hand-off links that flow downward with a subtle animated
  dash flow, and teammate-to-teammate message edges are curved arcs whose thickness scales with
  message weight and whose opacity scales with recency; same-row arcs bend upward so they clear the
  names. A structural hand-off graph is derived when a payload has no edge data.
- **Pixel-art agents.** Every member is drawn as a deterministic pixel-art character made of SVG
  rectangles from a 10x12 template (no external images): the Lead gets a distinct brand-colored outfit
  and marker, and the theme palette drives outfit accents. The working-ratio ring and token-scaled node
  radius are still there, with a tiny "N rounds · X tok" line under each node. Status motion: running
  bobs and shows a working spark, provisioning spins a dashed ring and blinks softly, idle is muted and
  static, failed keeps a static error ring.
- **Member details on hover or focus.** Hovering or focusing a node opens a compact detail card with
  the model, rounds, steps, token breakdown (uncached input, cache read, cache write, output, total),
  working and idle time, and the member's message in/out summary. Clicking the node opens the member's
  session when workspace navigation is available.
- **Compact task summary.** Each expanded team card shows one line with in-progress, pending, and
  blocked counts and a small expand toggle. Expanding shows only the in-progress tasks as one-line rows
  (subject, owner); pending and completed tasks stay counts only. Blocked follows the readiness rule:
  only a pending task with `ready === false` is blocked, and in-progress tasks are never shown as
  blocked.
- **Activity stays in the API.** The snapshot still carries the bounded activity list for API
  consumers, but the panel no longer renders it.
- **Interactive graph data.** When the host can see it, the snapshot also carries the member graph:
  structural Lead edges plus aggregated message edges from bounded member-session (live deliveries) and
  Lead-session (legacy records) scans. The panel remains read-only either way.
- **Multiple teams and projects.** One workspace card per live team in the grid, filtered by project
  when a project is selected.
- **Honest states.** A loading skeleton on first load, an error card with retry, a "showing the last
  successful snapshot" hint after a failed poll, an unsupported-service notice, and an empty state.
- **Bilingual.** All visible copy goes through the DSH client locale service, with Chinese and
  English dictionaries kept in sync; the panel follows the host language.
- **Theme-native.** Colors, borders, and pixel-art/graph art come only from `--dsw-*` theme tokens, so
  the panel follows dark and light themes. Graph nodes and cards are keyboard accessible and every
  animation (including the hand-off dash flow) is disabled under reduced motion.
- **Polling.** The panel refreshes a same-origin JSON snapshot every 2 seconds while it is mounted and
  the tab is visible, pauses while the tab is hidden, and offers a manual refresh button.
- **Optional navigation.** When the host exposes `uiWorkspace.openSession`, clicking a graph node
  opens that member's session. When it does not, the panel stays a read-only page.

## Requirements and compatibility

- **DSH Web UI** in the desktop app or a Web profile. The plugin was developed and tested against DSH
  `0.2.1-rc.2`; `package.json` declares `engines.dsh` as `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`, which also excludes
  0.3.0 prereleases.
- **The official experimental Agent Teams bundle must be mounted in the same profile.** This plugin
  visualizes teams that already exist; it does not provide the Agent Teams service itself. Without
  that service the panel shows a clear "not mounted" notice instead of failing.
- **Optional session projections.** Rounds, token usage, and working / idle times come from the stock
  DSH `sessionStats` and `tokenUsage` projections. They are optional: without them the panel still
  renders the graph and shows dashes for statistics.
- **A Web-capable profile.** The install examples below use the `desktop` profile; replace `desktop`
  with your own Web profile name (`web`, and so on) if it differs.
- **No separate Node.js installation is needed to use the plugin.** Node.js 22.19 or newer is only
  needed to run the tests in this repository.

## Install

The examples below use `dsh plugin --profile desktop add <spec>`. Replace `desktop` with your profile
name if you use a different Web profile.

### From the app Plugins page

1. Open **Plugins** in the DSH desktop app.
2. Choose **Add plugin**.
3. Paste `github:kkomia/dsh-agent-team-console` (or `dsh-agent-team-console` once the package is
   published

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex — native subagent progress, in-host worker sessions with per-tier presets, and a multimodal bridge that lends the text-only harness vision and image generation.

DSH Crew

A DeepSeek Harness plugin: dispatch work to DSH agents from Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok, without giving up the host's native subagent UI.
Native Progress UI • Tier Policy & Escalation • Dispatch Guardrails • Jobs Board • In-Host DSH Sessions • Vision & Image Gen (Native-First) • One-Click Install

npm: @zseven-w/dsh-crew · Current plugin release: 0.1.0-rc.11 · Tested with DSH 0.1.1-rc.1

English · 简体中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Français · Español · Deutsch · Português · Русский · हिन्दी · Türkçe · ไทย · Tiếng Việt · Bahasa Indonesia


The DSH Crew settings page — host integrations, dispatch policy, execution and the multimodal bridge

## Why DSH Crew DSH Crew is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) — an open-source agent harness. It makes DSH agents dispatchable from Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Grok: the orchestrator keeps its own model, the work runs on a real DSH agent with that harness's tools, sandbox, presets and session history, and the host still shows it as a native subagent with live progress. What runs the work is a DSH agent, not a bare model call. Tiers (`flash` / `pro`) select how much capability that agent gets from the harness's configured roster — DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro today — so a change of model in DSH needs no change here.
### 🧵 Native Progress UI Workers appear as regular subagents in Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok — dispatch count, running step, tool calls and token usage all show up in the host's own task panel, plus a claude-hud statusline segment: `⚙dsh 1▶pro 2m14s 21.7k/606 ✓3`. ### 🎚️ Tier Policy and Escalation `flash` for mechanical work, `pro` for reasoning, `effort` from `off` to `max`. `tier_policy` can clamp every dispatch to one tier at the tool layer, and `escalate_on_failure` retries a failed flash run once on pro — based on evidence, not on guessing difficulty up front.
### 🏛️ In-Host DSH Sessions With the bundle installed in a DSH profile, each worker is a first-class DSH session: visible in the Web UI, grouped by working directory, mounted with the Agent preset you choose per tier. Without DSH running, dispatch falls back to a standalone DSH runtime, so CI and headless environments still work. ### 👁️ Vision and Image Generation DSH's models are text-only. `describe_image` now prefers DeepSeek's own VL model (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`) whenever a key is available, then falls back to the CLIs you already have — Claude, Codex, Grok, Antigravity — or any OpenAI-compatible API you configure. `generate_image` borrows the same CLIs' brush. Pasted images stay visible in the conversation and reach the model as text.
### 🛡️ Dispatch Guardrails Every dispatch is checked before anything spawns. Worker→worker nesting is capped at origin-chain depth 3 and cycles are refused; a second worker on a workspace another job already holds is refused with the holder's info — never silently queued. Refusals are readable errors: wait or re-scope, don't bypass. ### 📋 Jobs Board The DSH Crew panel doubles as a jobs board: every worker job — running or finished — is listed with tier, effort, live progress and tokens, held workspaces show their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (e.g. a hub restart) is surfaced as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.
### 🔌 Custom Providers Bring your own endpoint (Base URL + API key + models) or a local command template. Each provider has a connectivity test that checks reachability and auth, then makes one real vision call so you find out now, not mid-task. ### 📦 One-Click Install The settings page installs and updates the Claude Code plugin, the Codex role files and the Antigravity / Grok agents, skills and commands for you — marketplace registration, permission allowlist, HUD wiring, absolute paths rendered for this machine — and restores them just as easily. Every settings file is backed up first.
## How it works ``` Claude Code / Codex / Antigravity / Grok (orchestrator, keeps its own model) └─ ds-flash / ds-pro ← native subagent shell (progress shows in the host's task UI) └─ MCP: dsh_run_worker(tier, effort, cwd, worker=) ├─ worker="agy"/"grok" → that external CLI runs the task (explicit opt-in) ├─ hub reachable → session inside DSH (visible in the Web UI, grouped by cwd) └─ otherwise → dsh-jsonrpc-agent runtime (worker.cordis.yml) └─ DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro (DSH SDK, event stream → progress and token stats) ``` ## One run, two views Dispatch fans out. Below, eighteen workers translate this README in parallel: the host counts them as its own subagents, while the harness runs them as real sessions.

Claude Code sees dsh-crew workers as native subagents, with a statusline segment tracking running tiers, elapsed time and tokens.

The DSH Crew panel sees the same run from the harness side: which host dispatched each job, its tier and effort, live progress and token usage.

The panel is also the jobs board: running and finished jobs stay listed with tier, progress and tokens, held workspaces name their holders, and a job that vanishes mid-flight (a hub restart) surfaces as an orphan ghost instead of disappearing silently.

## Install Install into a DSH profile from npm: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @zseven-w/dsh-crew@latest dsh web ``` Or, for local development straight from the source tree: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-crew dsh web ``` The `link:` protocol symlinks the profile dependency to this repository, so rebuilds are visible immediately. ### Configure DeepSeek credentials (standalone only) In hub mode — the installation above — workers run inside the DSH instance and use the DeepSeek credentials it is already configured with. Nothing else to set up. Only the standalone fallback needs a key of its own: dispatching from a host with no DSH instance running launches a worker runtime as a separate process. Obtain an API key from [platform.deepseek.com](https://platform.deepseek.com) and write it to `~/.config/dsh-crew/.env`: ``` DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-... ``` ### Verify ```bash node scripts/smoke.mjs ``` The smoke test dispatches one cheap job through whichever path is available — the hub when a DSH instance is running, s

plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-approval-ledger

Batch approvals with a risk gate and an auditable decision ledger for **DeepSeek Harness**.

> **Status: Sprint 1 Host code implemented and live-P0 verified in an isolated profile and the desktop profile.** `request_approvals`, the `/approvals` command, the `approval/request` hook, plan-review rendering, per-item selection, and the session-log audit fold are implemented and covered by tests. The package is **not published**; the default config is observe-only. Version is `0.1.0-beta.1`.

## Why

DSH asks for privileged operations one at a time. Because write/command tools are scheduled exclusively, the first approval blocks everything after it: you cannot collect future approvals without letting the agent declare them first.

This plugin adds:

- **One plan for a batch.** The agent submits `request_approvals`; you review a concise list and approve once.
- **Dependency stages.** Plan items can declare `dependsOn`; the matcher only unlocks a dependent item after its dependencies are consumed.
- **Risk gate.** Every actual call is re-classified. Critical operations are never auto-approved; high-risk ones need an explicit opt-in and a second confirmation; unknown ones stay manual.
- **Decision ledger.** Every auto/manual decision is traceable through the session log, plan-level `tool/result.meta`, and an in-memory per-call ledger; `/approvals audit` derives missing records from durable facts instead of guessing.
- **Official UI first.** The shipped approval card, question card, and plan card are not replaced.

In the current observe-only configuration the plan is reviewed, but each actual call still uses the official approval card; grants are simulated and audited as `would-allow`. Active medium-risk auto-approval is the next release step.

## Safety model

- `critical` is **never** auto-approved.
- `unknown` is always manual.
- Auto-approval requires **two gates**: the plan scope matches **and** the actual call is risk-eligible.
- Path matching resolves symlinks/junctions to the real target and treats hard-linked files as high risk (manual).
- Grants are in-memory, session-scoped, and turn-scoped; they disappear on turn end, unload, or restart.
- Any exception, parse failure, or mismatch falls back to the official approval UI.
- The audit store never records full arguments, commands, reasons, or secrets.

## Install

Installed locally with `link:` into a temporary profile and the desktop profile for live P0. The npm package is **not published yet**; the command below is the planned install path once the release security review is approved.

```sh
# planned
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-approval-ledger
```

## Sprint 0 core

The host-side core is dependency-free and does not import DSH types:

- `normalizePath` / `matchPathScope` — case-normalized absolute paths, realpath of the nearest existing ancestor, hard-link detection, UNC/ADS/8.3/device-name rejection, and directory-only containment.
- `normalizeCommand` / `matchCommandScope` — whitespace normalization plus hard rejection of shell metacharacters, interpreters, script files, downloads, and encoded commands from automatic matching.
- `matchArgsScope` — bounded JSON validation and exact-subset matching; arrays must match exactly.
- `assessRisk` — deterministic, advisory levels and reasons; `critical` and `unknown` never auto-approve.
- `validatePlan` — unique ids, acyclic dependencies, stage computation, use limits, normalized scopes, risk counts, and a stable plan hash.
- `AuditLedger` / `replayAudit` / `renderAuditReport` — metadata-only records, hash/scrub summaries, append-only sequencing, and replay that marks missing or conflicting evidence instead of guessing.

## Sprint 1 Host wiring

- `request_approvals` registers a plain DSH tool definition and asks one official plan-review question; after approval it asks a second multi-select question so you can authorize only the items you want. Unchecked items stay manual.
- The client half adds a localized **Approval details** button to the session header, with a red dot for a pending approval and a read-only modal showing the Host-rewritten summary and original reason. It never answers the approval.
- On Windows, the Host can flash the DeepSeek Harness window when an official approval card is actually waiting. It is best-effort, opt-out (`flashWindow: false`), and never blocks or changes the decision.
- Grants are installed in memory per `(session, turn)`; the prepended `approval/request` hook applies the plan gate and the per-call risk gate, and rewrites the card's `displayReason` to a real mode + target summary.
- Observe mode (the default) consumes the simulated grant and records `would-allow`, but never returns `allowed-once`.
- `/approvals [audit [--json] | grants]` folds durable session events plus plan metadata; missing per-call records are derived from `tool/call` arguments and marked `derived-session-log`, never guessed.
- `ctx.storageDomain` is a schema-validated KV store, not an append-only log; Sprint 1 deliberately uses the session log + in-memory ledger instead. Cross-session retention is deferred.

## Development

Requirements: Node.js 22+, pnpm.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

`pnpm test` compiles `src/` and `test/` to `lib-test/` and runs Node's built-in test runner. `pnpm build` emits the Host half to `lib/`.

The package is a Cordis bundle: `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `approval-ledger` row; `lib/index.js` is the Host half.

## Documentation

- [Design](docs/design.md)
- [Threat model](docs/threat-model.md)
- [Audit / decision ledger](docs/audit.md)
- [Runtime notes](docs/runtime-notes.md)
- [Runtime spike (0.2.1-rc.2)](docs/runtime-spike.md)
- [Compatibility](docs/compatibility.md)
- [Handoff](HANDOFF.md)

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

## Disclaimer

Unofficial community plugin. Not affiliated with DeepSeek. Do not use the DeepSeek name or logo to imply endorsement.
